Datatable.LocalizationPair: Empire traits signifying use of Eldritch, forbidden, and dangerous methods

This empire has employed eldritch methods of traveling faster and reaching farther by slipping through alternate geometries. Its operatives ride the same impossible angles into foreign networks, sustaining an additional hacking operation.

The structural lattice of this Crescent murmurs constantly in a language no one taught it. Little of it survives transcription — but let the whispers ride an intrusion into a foreign network, and they arrive early, knowing the passwords.
Dust seeps upward through this Crescent's floor from a place that, by every measurement, is not there. Accountants have learned not to ask where the ledger balances from.
Something in the hollow spaces of this Crescent sings the Choir's song back — a half-beat late, and very slightly wrong. Outsiders find the effect magnetic. Residents find it hard to sleep.
Taught the true song at last, the presence in the hollow spaces now sings in perfect unison with the Choir. The duet is the loveliest sound in the galaxy, and only slightly older than it.
In certain corridors of this Crescent, shifts end before they begin and quotas fill themselves in hours that do not exist. The crops, unfortunately, also experience seasons that do not exist.
The folds have been charted, scheduled, and unionized. Work now flows through the impossible hours without losing so much as a harvest, and the overtime paperwork is filed yesterday.
Something feeds in the non-space between this Crescent's angles. Meals go missing. Ideas go missing. The corners of rooms are wider than they should be, and getting wider.

Fed deliberately and well, the thing between the angles has begun leaving gifts: answers to unasked questions, Dust in tidy stacks, and a contentment that settles over the Crescent like a warm shadow.
+5 Experience per turn on the Hero assigned to this System
Allows the teleportation of fleets between this system and another portal
Teach the mimic the true song, note by patient note, until it sings with the Choir instead of at it.
Chart every impossible hour and put it on the schedule. Time is only a problem for those who insist on experiencing it in order.
Stop rationing what it takes and start offering what it wants. A fed god is a friendly god, or at least a generous one.
